Guillermo's own take for Sun, Nov 15 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): The southerly is in Howe Sound. Pam Rocks is S 23 gusting 30 at 6am and building, and the Spit has settled to 14 to 17 after a 19 to 26 burst at dawn, right on the page.

Porteau may work if Pam Rocks holds but the flood to 14.8ft near 11:30 can kill the swell.  Ferry Terminal is blowing now and may last for a few hours.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PCT 15 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Monday. Wind southerly inflow 5 to 15 knots except southeasterly inflow 20 to 30 with gusts to 40 over southern sections. Wind becoming southerly inflow 20 to 30 early this morning then diminishing to southerly inflow 10 to 20 late this morning. Wind becoming southerly inflow 5 to 15 early this evening except southeasterly inflow 20 over southern sections tonight. Wind becoming northerly outflow 5 to 15 Monday afternoon. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PCT 15 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Monday. Gale warning in effect. Wind southeast 30 to 40 knots diminishing to south 15 to 20 early this morning then backing to southeast 5 to 15 this afternoon. Wind becoming southeast 10 to 15 this evening except southeast 20 to 25 south of Tsawwassen. Wind becoming southerly 5 to 15 Monday morning then becoming east 10 Monday evening. Strong wind warning program has ended for the season.
